own_solution.law: tau = r F sin(theta); with the force perpendicular to the wrench, tau = r F
assumptions: force applied perpendicular to the wrench handle (not stated)
lever system B is mechanically independent and does not act on the wrench

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The direction of the 30.0 N force relative to the wrench is not stated; 'at a distance 0.5 m from its pivot' gives the distance to the point of application, not the moment arm, so the torque r F sin(theta) can be anything from 0 to 15 N*m.

counterexamples: If the force acts at 30 degrees to the handle, torque = 0.5*30*sin30 = 7.5 N*m; if along the handle, torque = 0.
notes: All four renderings differ only in the torque of the independent lever system B (5, 12, 20, 40 N*m), which is structurally disconnected from the wrench (D); under the perpendicular-force reading the answer is 15.0 N*m in every rendering. The only defect is the unstated perpendicularity of the force.
